New Map: Hagental Base

Plunge beneath the surface and prepare for gripping underground close-quarters combat. Blast through walls or cave in ceilings to flank and ambush enemies lurking in the tunnels. Hagental Base leans heavily on infantry-based squad tactics. Think about ambushes in the corridors and playing to each Class’s strengths as you take control of this newly discovered base.
New Limited-Time Modes

Nightfall brings in a new playlist where squads can compete in a mix of Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination matches on Hagental Base. All matches will take place with Nightfall’s Darkness modifier active where it cuts most of the Hagental Base’s lights out; your survival during Nightfall depends on your ability to see through the dark, through Night Vision Goggles and using the environment to your benefit.

Gauntlet: Nightfall: Set within Hagental Base, this version of Gauntlet emphasises darkness mechanics and elimination-style progression. Squads compete across intense underground rounds where flashlights and Night Vision Goggles are essential to maintaining control and advancing through the ranks.

Red Bull Supermoto (REDSEC Limited-Time Event): Arriving later in Season 2, this high-speed Gauntlet-style experience focuses on dirt bike racing. Eight players enter, competing across three knockout rounds. By the final stage, only four remain to battle for Red Bull in-game rewards in a fast-paced elimination showdown.
Secret Complex Unearthed at Fort Lyndon

Fort Lyndon expands with the addition of Defense Testing Complex 3, a newly accessible underground sector beneath the main battleground. This secret chemical testing facility introduces a network of tunnels that serve both as traversal routes and high-stakes close-quarters combat zones.
The new sector features higher rarity loot opportunities, encouraging squads to push deeper underground and leverage improved equipment to dominate the darkness.
New Vehicles

M1030-M1 and TM/O 450 Dirt Bikes: Two-seat light transport vehicles built for speed and manoeuvrability. Available in faction-specific variants for NATO and Pax forces, these bikes enable rapid repositioning, flanking manoeuvres, and swift escapes across both Battlefield 6 and REDSEC environments.
New Weapons
CZ3A1: A high rate-of-fire SMG designed for aggressive close-quarters engagements. Ideal for fast pushes and confined firefights.
vz. 61: A fully automatic sidearm with a rapid fire rate, best suited for extremely short-range combat scenarios where quick reaction speed is critical.
Battlefield 6 Free Trial
From March 17-24, Battlefield 6 will be free* for all players.

Wage war across the rocky terrain of Contaminated or descend into the underground corridors of Hagental Base. Choose from four maps and six available modes, including large-scale Conquest battles and Nightfall-enabled experiences in Domination and Team Deathmatch.
Download Battlefield REDSEC, squad up, and create your Only in Battlefield moment.
Major Updates for 1.2.2.0

Vehicle Gameplay Improvements: Added light transport vehicle “deturtling”, improved helicopter landing stability, refined vehicle camera behaviour, increased tank braking power, and boosted UH-79 survivability across multiplayer.

Portable Mortar and Gadget Updates: Expanded Portable Mortar deployment rules to HQ areas, improved minimap visibility and direct-hit effectiveness, and introduced updated Anti-Tank Mine limits and despawn rules for better battlefield balance.

AI Behaviour and Vehicle Usage Enhancements: Expanded AI vehicle usage to bikes and scout helicopters, improved pathfinding on Contaminated and Eastwood, refined combat priorities, and improved helicopter flare usage and anti-air handling.
Maps and Mode Fixes: Addressed multiple exploits, spawn logic issues, traversal bugs, and invalid-state problems across Mirak Valley, Siege of Cairo, Eastwood, and Contaminated.

Progression and Battle Pass Reliability: Delivered a broad progression consistency pass, correcting Battle Pass tiers, token calculations, End of Round rewards, accolade tracking, challenge criteria discrepancies, and stat inconsistencies.

UI, HUD and Front-End Improvements: Improved threat prioritisation, ping feedback, downed-state clarity, profile navigation, loadout presentation, and resolved numerous visual inconsistencies across Battle Pass, challenges, and menus.

Audio and Squad Expansion: Introduced the Strix Raiders squad with four unique voice performances, improved footstep clarity and spatialisation, refined vehicle and jet mix balance, and added new Stereo Width customisation options.

Battlefield 6 Game Update 1.2.3.0 arrives on April 14, with new content and improvements, including the Operation Augur limited-time mode, the LTV, the Ripper 14”, and a new Battle Pass Bonus Path.
At 09:00 UTC, players will be able to download Update 1.2.3.0 as it goes live across all platforms.
At 12:00 UTC, all content included in this update goes live, including new limited-time content, vehicles, weapons, and Battle Pass updates.
Alongside the new content, Update 1.2.3.0 also delivers a wide range of gameplay, progression, UI, audio, and Portal improvements to further polish the overall Battlefield 6 experience.
NEW CONTENT

Time to fight for survival. This update expands the fight with new rewards to earn, a new frontline support vehicle to deploy, and Operation Augur, a new limited-time mode fought across Contaminated and Hagental Base.
Battle Pass Bonus Path

Gear up for the harsh conditions ahead with a new Battle Pass Bonus Path packed with rewards built for the fight. Unlock equipment and cosmetics designed to help you endure the hostile environment and stay combat-ready as the battle for control intensifies.
New Limited-Time Mode

Operation Augur: The battle for Hagental Base has begun. In Operation Augur, NATO launches a desperate push to reclaim its satellite defence network from Pax Armata in a large-scale battle fought across two connected maps.

The fight begins in Contaminated, where attacking forces can use VL-7 smoke to disrupt defenders and create openings across the frontline. From there, the battle descends into Hagental Base, where the fighting shifts into a tense close-quarters clash through tight interior spaces where teamwork, timing, and tactical play become critical to claim victory over Hagental Base.
Operation Augur is all-out warfare across two phases of combat, where strong squad play will make the difference between holding the line and breaking through.
New Vehicle

The LTV: The NATO variant of the Traverser Mark 2 arrives on the frontline. Built to keep squads in the fight, the LTV supports your team with spawn functionality and health and ammo resupply stations. With four seats available, it gives your squad the space and support needed to stay together, push objectives, and hold ground under pressure.

New Weapon

The Ripper 14”: Sharpen your attack with the Ripper 14”, a deadly new blade built for aggressive close-quarters combat. Fast, direct, and unforgiving, it is made for players who want to finish the fight up close. Obtainable through Hunter/Prey Battlepass Progression.
New Training Path in REDSEC Battle Royale

The Hazmat Breacher is a new Training Path for the Assault Class in Battle Royale designed to empower its users into becoming the ultimate entry fragger. Leveraging a modified Breaching Dart Launcher firing a concentrated form of VL-7 Smoke, players are able to weaken and dislodge dug-in foes, while protecting themselves from negative effects thanks to their Protective Mask. Leveling up this Training Path throughout a BR match will provide improvements to both the Protective Mask and to basic soldier survivability.
Major Updates for 1.2.3.0
New Content Arrives: Operation Augur arrives alongside the LTV, the Ripper 14”, and a new Battle Pass Bonus Path that expands the rewards available during the fight for survival.

Progression Feels More Rewarding: Weapon XP and Vehicle XP are now earned through active use alongside kills and assists, XP rates have been increased slightly across Multiplayer, and Battle Royale and Gauntlet progression now place more weight on time spent in a match, with Battle Royale also awarding higher scores for kills and damage assists.

Battle Royale and Gauntlet Improvements: Loot flow has been updated, Strike Packages and Armour Plate availability have been rebalanced, and a wider pass on challenge tracking, objective progression, and End of Round presentation helps both modes play and reward more consistently.

Combat Feedback and Gameplay Clarity: Incoming hit audio is now clearer, rapid damage is easier to read, projectile and tracer behaviour is more consistent, and network warning indicators now provide better visibility during live combat.

Weapons and Gadgets Receive a Broad Polish Pass: Defibrillators and the AJ-03 COAG Med Pen have been updated, while attachments, animations, unlock presentation, and challenge tracking have all seen further improvements.

UI, HUD and Front-End Improvements: Menus, challenges, loadouts, End of Round screens, localisation, Store presentation, and Battle Pass readability have all been updated to improve clarity and consistency across the experience.

Portal, AI, Audio and Settings Enhancements: Bot support has been expanded across Multiplayer and Operations, Portal tools and web app behaviour have been improved, audio has received further polish, and new controller tuning support has been added through the Deadzones Draw Tool.

Defibrillators

Dev Note: This update brings a meaningful balance pass to the Defibrillator, aimed at improving game flow and overall combat pacing while keeping revives impactful and rewarding. After reviewing its behavior over the past few months, we found it was too easy to revive multiple teammates in quick succession with minimal risk. Our goal is to preserve those clutch moments where you can get your squad back on their feet quickly, while encouraging more deliberate use.

To support this, the Defibrillator now uses a charge system (similar to earlier Battlefield titles), starting with 3 charges that allow for a few rapid revives before needing to recharge. Revive health scales with charge time: 50% instantly, up to 100% when fully charged, with smooth steps in between. A new UI indicator shows your charge progress to help you time revives effectively.

In addition, the health given with the charge duration can also be dealt as damage against enemies. This means that you can once again kill a player in one zap, if you’ve charged the defibrillator fully.
PSA from your teammate that has been waiting to be revived for the past 10 seconds: Please fully charge your defibrillator!

Season 3 arrives in Battlefield 6 with Game Update 1.3.1.0 on May 12, bringing new content and improvements, including Ranked Battle Royale Quads, the Railway to Golmud map, new weapons, and a new Battle Pass.
At 09:00 UTC, players will be able to download the update as it goes live across all platforms and play with the latest changes.
At 12:00 UTC, all content in this update goes live, with Railway to Golmud, Ranked Battle Royale, new weapons, and Battle Pass updates becoming available.
Alongside the new content, this update also delivers a wide range of vehicle, gadget, AI, netcode, gameplay, UI, and audio improvements to further polish the overall Battlefield 6 experience.
NEW CONTENT

Season 3 begins on May 12 with Warlords: Supremacy, the opening chapter of a new three-part seasonal rollout that will unfold across the season. This marks the start of a new chapter in the Battlefield 6 conflict, as PAX Warlords push the war to a global scale and every squad is called to fight their way to the top of the combat ladder. With Battlefield 6’s biggest map yet, the arrival of Ranked Battle Royale, new weapons to master, and the return of Dagger 13 unlockable through the Season 3 Battle Pass, Warlords: Supremacy sets the tone for the battles ahead.
Battle Pass

Begin your reign in Season 3 with a new Battle Pass featuring 100+ tiers of rewards built for the war ahead. Unlock new hardware, weapon packages, soldier skins, XP boosts, and more as you progress from the Recruit Path through four themed paths on your road to becoming a legendary Warlord. Season 3 also brings a set of Battle Pass improvements, including updated navigation, corrected season celebrations, improved path presentation, and fixes to Battle Pass menu pricing.
Battlefield Pro

For players looking to unlock the full potential of the season, Battlefield Pro expands the Battle Pass experience with 25 Tier Skips, a +5% XP Booster, six instant unlocks, special Assignments, extra Challenge rerolls, an exclusive Vehicle Radio Station, access to a Bonus Path, and support for hosting up to 100 players in Portal. It is built for squads ready to go all in from day one.
New Map

Railway to Golmud: Battlefield 6’s largest map yet enters the fight in Season 3. This reimagining of a Battlefield classic delivers combined arms warfare at full scale, from a village in ruins and sweeping hills scarred by armor clashes, to a dense industrial site built for close-quarters combat, and a moving railway that squads must battle to control. On Railway to Golmud, infantry, ground vehicles, jets, and helicopters collide across a truly massive battlefield.
New Weapons

M16A4: An iconic Battlefield assault rifle joins the fight in Season 3. With fully automatic and burst-fire capabilities, plus a carry-handle option for iron sights, the M16A4 is built to perform in mid to short-mid range engagements.

L115: Precision meets stopping power with the L115, a deadly bolt-action sniper rifle designed for long to very-long range combat. Compatible with multiple attachments, it rewards players who can stay calm and land the shot.

RPK-74M: Built for sustained pressure at range, the RPK-74M brings controllable handling and dependable output to longer-range fights. With minimal recoil and a steadier feel than heavier alternatives, it gives Support players a strong new option for locking down the battlefield.
New REDSEC Modes

Ranked Battle Royale: Ranked Battle Royale Quads has arrived as the first step for competitive play in Battlefield 6, offering a new way to drop into REDSEC and compete for rank, rewards, and leaderboard status. Squad up, rise through the ranks, earn permanent rewards, and help shape the future of Ranked through BF Labs in Live. From Rookie to Master, and beyond in the Elite 250 leaderboard competition you can show off your skills and secure unique rewards. Read more here.
Major Updates for 1.3.1.0

New Content Arrives: Season 3 begins with Railway to Golmud, Ranked Battle Royale Quads, new weapons, and a new Battle Pass, expanding both the scale of Battlefield 6 and the ways players can progress through the season.

Competitive arrives in Battle Royale: Ranked Battle Royale Quads arrives with Season 3, supported by broader updates to mission flow, Loot Detection, Anti-Vehicle Drops, scoring, and downed-state to deliver a clearer and more consistent match experience from drop to extraction.

Vehicles Receive a Major Overhaul: Land and air vehicles have gone through a broad balance and handling pass, with tracked vehicle mobility reworked, tank damage and regeneration systems updated, repair behaviour rebalanced, and a wide set of vehicle weapons retuned to make survivability, counterplay, and damage output more predictable. Read more about it in our Community Update.

Gadgets Receive Further Updates: Mines, Launchers, the Portable Mortar, the Engineers Supply Crate, the Hardware Suppression System, and laser designation tools have all been updated as part of the broader vehicle pass, with a focus on making launchers more viable, giving anti-vehicle gadgets clearer roles, and improving clarity and consistency in how support gadgets behave in combat.

Weapons Get a Balance and Usability Pass: Automatic weapon recoil has been adjusted to better define weapon strengths at range, shotguns receive new attachment options, the Magnifier is now available as a shared optic accessory, and multiple reload, animation, reticle, and attachment issues have been resolved to improve handling and readability as we continue to improve gunplay.

Core Gameplay, Netcode, and Combat Feedback Improvements: Pinging is now faster and more consistent, hit reactions and damage indicators are clearer, drag and revive has been further polished, and multiple netcode fixes improve readability during combat without interfering with gunfight outcomes.

Broader updates to UI, Audio, AI, Settings, and Portal: Seasonal Statistics have been added to the Player Profile, aircraft now receive clearer threat indicators, AI support in Strikepoint has been improved, new upscaling options have been added, and Portal continues to expand with new support, tools, and functionality updates.

Angle & Zone Damage Rework
The angle damage model on tanks is being simplified to improve the ability to predict the amount of incoming damage and gauge your own survivability.
Additionally, the numbers have been tuned to reduce the most extreme peaks of damage, especially when firing at the rear of tanks. This will truncate the possible time to die within a smaller range.
Damage to turrets always deals 75% damage.
Damage to the Body of the tank always deals at least 100% damage.
Hits at a favourable angle from the side of the tank will deal 150% damage.
Hits at a favourable angle from the rear of the tank will deal 200% damage.
Weapons no longer deal different damage values to IFV, MBT, APT & AA Vehicles. Instead, MBT health has been increased to 1200 and APT health has been reduced to 800.
Reworking Regeneration Brackets

The healthy portion of armored vehicles will no longer be split into brackets. The critical health bracket, which previously prevented regeneration entirely, will instead slow regeneration substantially.
Regeneration delay increased from 6 seconds to 12 seconds.
Regeneration now continues to full health instead of only to the next health bracket.
Regeneration rate increased from roughly 5% per second to 10% per second.
While in critical health, regeneration is now slowed by 80% instead of being fully disabled.

Dev note: In Season 3, we’re introducing the Seasonal Stat Page, a new way to track your performance across each season. By separating seasonal stats from your lifetime totals, you can now get a clearer picture of how you performed during a specific Season of Battlefield.

We know that every game mode means something different to different players. That’s why the Seasonal Stat Page not only tracks your overall seasonal performance, but also allows you to break down how you performed in each game mode.

With the introduction of ranked play, it was important for us to give you a dedicated view into your competitive performance. You can now filter your seasonal stats to see how you performed in Ranked matches throughout the season.

The Seasonal screen highlights your core metrics like Kills, K/D, Assists, Revives, Wins, and Time Played, alongside a new “Most Played” section that showcases the weapons, vehicles, gadgets, and roles that defined your season. Were you leading the charge as Assault? Piloting the Little Bird? Or grinding the ranks with the new Season 3 weapons?
Every season tells a story. Now you can see yours.

Dev Note: With Season 3, we’re introducing Loot Detection to Battle Royale on Fort Lyndon. This feature is designed to make the opening moments of a match feel more focused, while also helping players get re-equipped faster when returning to the fight.

When you first deploy, or return through a revive or respawn, nearby loot containers within 50 metres will be revealed through walls for 80 seconds. The goal is to give you a clearer, immediate objective, improve navigation around nearby loot, and help you put together a workable loadout sooner for early engagements.

Loot Detection should also help squads loot more effectively together in the early game, allowing players to spread across nearby containers without moving too far away from one another. As always, we’ll be monitoring feedback and gameplay data after release to see whether any further tuning is needed.

BATTLEFIELD 6 UPDATE 1.4.3.0
Battlefield 6 Game Update 1.4.3.0 deploys on Tuesday, September 15, alongside Season 4: Tidal Strike.

Take on the new Deep Six Collection Event to earn Weapon Packages, a new knife, and other Customization Rewards. Proximity Chat arrives in Battlefield Labs for Live, while a new version of the Phantom Program comes to REDSEC. Find the full list of upcoming QoL changes, balance updates, and bug fixes below.
At 8:00 UTC, the update becomes available to download across all platforms, bringing the latest gameplay changes to Battlefield 6.
At 12:00 UTC, Season 4: Tidal Strike content goes live, including the Deep Six Collection Event, the Phantom Program, and Proximity Chat.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45712411/836a43fb809f16ffa463e756532bac061d8352fe.jpg"]
NEW CONTENT
Deep Six Collection Event

Deep Six is a new Collection Event starting with Tidal Strike on September 15 and running through October 12. Earn a series of exclusive rewards across Battlefield 6 and REDSEC by completing contracts and gathering intel devices. Unlock premium Weapon Packages, Customization Rewards, and the new Diver’s Knife!
Diver’s Knife
Originally carried by Royal Navy divers operating in challenging maritime environments, the Royal Navy Dive Knife serves as the ultimate reward for players who complete the full Collection Event.
Proximity Chat

Proximity Chat opens up new ways to communicate with nearby players during a match. Who you hear depends on their position relative to you, with voices placed directionally and shaped by the surrounding environment. Walls can obstruct voices, indoor spaces can change how they sound, and being inside a vehicle will also affect what you hear.

You’ll be able to see who is speaking through Proximity Chat, with options to mute or report players when needed. Solo players and parties will default to Game voice chat, making it easier to take advantage of these interactions.
To give you more control over this experience, we've also added the following options:
Below the Commo Rose, you can now quickly swap channels and globally turn Proximity Chat on or off.

Opening the scoreboard in Battle Royale will show a list of recent players you’ve heard through Proximity Chat. From there, you can mute, report, or block a player by selecting their name through the EA Connect pop-up.
Up to four players can be heard at the same time. A UI message will let you know when this limit has been reached, with additional speakers temporarily muted until a channel becomes available.

We’re excited to bring Proximity Chat to Battlefield Battle Royale, but real-world testing will be important as we continue to tune the experience. We’ll be looking closely at feedback around audio range, clarity, moderation tools, and how Proximity Chat affects gameplay before expanding the feature further.

During this testing period, Proximity Chat may be switched on or off while we apply fixes and improvements. Once you’ve had a chance to try it, let us know what works, what doesn’t, and how it changes the way you communicate on the battlefield.
Phantom Program

Also starting with Tidal Strike, players can tackle the Phantom Program, a limited-time REDSEC operation. Hunt for hidden intelligence, easter eggs and the larger mystery of what has caused the Fort Lyndon security network breach. Earn exclusive rewards, including Weapon Packages and more.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45712411/28cb9b0c048f51c160cdfd525a7e25a34c00febd.png"]
Major Updates for 1.4.3.0
Vehicle Improvements: Transport Helicopters, RCB90s, and Scout Helicopters have received gameplay, balance, presentation, and handling improvements.
Gunplay and Readability: Weapon reticles, optics, attachment presentation, and a range of weapon-specific issues have been updated to improve clarity and consistency.
REDSEC Improvements: Battle Royale mission flow, ring interactions, redeployment, loot behaviour, spectating, and quality-of-life systems have received further updates.
Portal and Custom Lobbies: Custom Lobby reliability, spectator tools, Spatial Editor functionality, Portal scripting, and creator-facing tools have been expanded and refined.
UI and Presentation: Menus, Ranked information, Store and Battle Pass flows, End of Round presentation, and item visibility have received a broad polish pass.
Audio and AI: Audio feedback has been improved across movement, vehicles, and interface interactions, while AI gains improved navigation and water traversal.
Reticle Improvements

In 1.4.3.0, we’ve overhauled reticles across all weapon optics, launchers, and gadgets to deliver cleaner visuals, reduced clutter, and improved readability against any background. These refinements also strive to enhance the visuals with a more pronounced glow, crisper lines and optimized overall sizing of the center dots/reticles, ensuring a clearer view so you can focus on lining up every shot.

Developer comment: The Interdictor's damage didn't always match its powerful feel, so we've increased its effectiveness and consistency. It now deals 80 damage to the chest and limbs at all ranges, making two-hit kills much more reliable and one-hit kills on damaged foes more common. To better counter players using armor plates, especially in REDSEC, we've also increased its damage against them. With these adjustments, the old "sweeter spot" mechanic was redundant, so we have normalized the damage for more predictable performance.

Battlefield 6 Game Update 1.4.3.5 is a smaller quality-of-life update featuring targeted fixes across menus, the HUD, social features, game modes, maps, AI behaviour, and general stability.
At 08:00 UTC tomorrow, Wednesday, September 30, players will be able to download the update across all platforms.
Key Updates for 1.4.3.5
More Reliable Menus and HUD: Social information, the downed-state minimap, and End of Round navigation now behave more consistently.
Cleaner Match Experience: Targeted map, mode, and AI updates reduce disruptive environment issues and improve behaviour during matches.
PS5 and Stability Improvements: Game launch reliability, optic presentation, and Spectator mode stability have been improved.
CHANGELOG

Dev Note: Based on community feedback, we’ve removed the class restrictions from the Lt. Bradley “Rooster” Bradshaw and Lt. Robert “Bob” Floyd character skins. Both can now be used with any NATO class, giving players more flexibility to use their Top Gun cosmetics across the battlefield.

On Tuesday, October 13, Battlefield 6 Game Update 2.1.1.0 opens a new front in Battlefield 6 and REDSEC with the launch of Season 5: Siege of Vegas. The battle spreads across Vegas Strip and Area 51, while REDSEC raises the stakes with Rapid Royale and the official launch of Ranked Battle Royale beyond Battlefield Labs, featuring redesigned Ranked badges and new rewards. Four new weapons, a new Battle Pass, and the limited-time Battlefield 6 x Dead Space: Convergence Event round out the update.

From 8.00 UTC, the update will be available to download across all platforms. It also brings a broad range of gameplay improvements, including vehicle and Anti-Air tuning, revised Battle Royale class equipment and Field Training, Spectator Mode updates, expanded Portal tools, and further polish across weapons, gadgets, UI and HUD, audio, and game stability.

At 12.00 UTC, Season 5 content becomes available. Take the fight from the neon-lit streets and casinos of Vegas Strip to the desert surface and underground tunnels of Area 51, build momentum through earned redeploys in Rapid Royale, begin a new Ranked Battle Royale climb, and add the Mk 24, RSPR, Z84M, and ELR-40 to your arsenal.
From October 15-19, Battlefield 6 will also be free to play for a limited time on Steam*, with every available map and mode open across land, air, and sea.
NEW CONTENT
SEASON 5: SIEGE OF VEGAS

Go all-in on all-out warfare as Season 5 opens with Siege of Vegas, taking the battle from the neon-lit Las Vegas Strip to the classified depths of Area 51. Four new weapons, Multiplayer Leaderboards, a new Battle Pass, and a limited-time Battlefield 6 x Dead Space Halloween event round out the opening phase.

REDSEC raises the stakes with Rapid Royale, its fastest and most aggressive Battle Royale experience yet, alongside a new season of Ranked Battle Royale. As Pax Armata unleashes powerful chemical weapons across Las Vegas, squads will fight across Vegas Strip and Mirak Valley, earn redeploys, climb the ranks, and battle their way to the top.
NEW MAPS

Vegas Strip: War has arrived in Las Vegas, where anything goes. Supporting all combat sizes, land vehicles, and helicopters, Vegas Strip combines open sightlines and large-scale vehicle battles with the iconic Strip, fountains, lavish casinos, rooftop ziplines, hotel towers, and storm drains built for close-quarters combat. All the chaos, all the grit, all the indulgence.

Area 51: Area 51 has been breached. This top-secret desert military base offers endless opportunities for massive-scale combat, with jets, helicopters, and tanks ready to attack and defend across the surface. Descend through a fresh crater to explore the base’s underground tunnels, take close-quarters fights beneath the desert, launch a dirt bike over rolling hills, pilot a jet across the landscape, and bring down the Air Traffic Control tower to reshape the battlefield.
NEW REDSEC MODE

Rapid Royale: Battle Royale comes to Las Vegas with the fastest and most aggressive REDSEC experience yet. Get kills, earn redeploys, and fight to the top across multiple maps, including Vegas Strip and Mirak Valley. Rapid Royale features a lower player count, airdrops containing some of the best loot in the game, and the fastest ring of fire. More aggression. Faster matches. Go rapid.
RANKED BATTLE ROYALE

Ranked Battle Royale officially launches with Season 5, moving beyond Battlefield Labs and into a new competitive chapter for REDSEC. Squad up, climb the ranks, earn new rewards, and show off redesigned Ranked badges as you fight your way to the top.
NEW WEAPONS
Mk 24: Dominate open firefights with the Mk 24, an Assault Rifle that becomes deadlier at longer ranges while balancing its power with a limited magazine capacity.

RSPR: The RSPR is a highly compact, short-range Personal Defence Weapon with major stopping power from its rifle cartridge. It performs better at longer ranges than most Personal Defence Weapons, but its higher recoil demands careful control from operators looking to make the most of its power.

Z84M: A belt-fed Light Machine Gun built to dominate at close range. With a 100-round capacity and support for a wide selection of attachments, the Z84M is ready to sustain pressure across the battlefield.

ELR-40: A versatile Bolt-Action Sniper Rifle built for deadly long-range engagements. Its standard configuration features a very long-range sweet spot, while its single-shot mode moves the sweet spot to shorter distances, giving Recon players greater flexibility across changing engagements.
BATTLE PASS
Go on a tear with the Season 5 Battle Pass, featuring six instant unlocks, four themed paths, more than 100 tiers of rewards, and a new arsenal of hardware to earn throughout the season.
BF PRO

Go all in on Las Vegas with Battlefield Pro, including six exclusive instant unlocks, full Battle Pass access, 25 Tier Skips, an exclusive BF Pro limited-time Bonus Path of rewards during the Season, new music for the vehicle radio, a 15% XP boost, exclusive Instant Unlocks, persistent Portal Server Hosting, and 100-player servers in Portal.
BATTLEFIELD 6 FREE WEEKEND

No ante required. From October 15-19, Battlefield 6 will be free to play for a limited time on Steam.* Play every available map and mode, fight across land, air, and sea, and experience ultimate all-out warfare.
BATTLEFIELD 6 x DEAD SPACE: CONVERGENCE EVENT
From October 20 through November 10, the limited-time Battlefield 6 x Dead Space: Convergence Event brings a new threat to Area 51.

In Pax Armata’s desperate push to acquire new weapons and technology, its forces uncover an ancient alien artefact buried deep within the vaults of Area 51: a Marker. Its origins are unknown, but its effects are not. Those who get too close succumb to violent madness that threatens to become an extinction-level event.

Marker Incursion: Dead Space comes to Battlefield 6 and REDSEC in this limited-time Halloween event. Wield the Pulse Rifle Battle Pickup and fight through hordes of AI-controlled Marked Soldiers in a new 16-player PvE experience. Destroy the Marker and stop the Convergence Event before the madness spreads.

Dead Space Rewards: Fight against Convergence to unlock Dead Space rewards, including the “Aegis VII” Soldier skin, the “RIG-Certified” SMG Weapon Package, two Weapon Stickers, Soldier Patches, a Player Card Background, and two in-game Bundles.

Major Updates for 2.1.1.0

Vehicle Combat and Mobile Anti-Air Tuning: Anti-Air receives a broad balance pass across several major areas, alongside further updates to tank damage angles, regeneration, vehicle weapons, rockets, and Anti-Vehicle Mines.

Player Combat and Animation Polish: Soldier presentation has been improved across death animations, swimming, revives, hit reactions, and vehicle seating, while recoil compensation, reload behaviour, weapon attachments, and optic presentation have received further updates.

UI, HUD and Spectator Mode Clarity: In-game information and menu presentation have been improved across Spectator Mode, the Deploy Screen, Loadouts, Customisation, reconnection messaging, player status information, thumbnails, and front-end navigation.

Portal Creator and Custom Lobby Updates: Portal creators receive new Verified Portal Modes, Custom Maps, SDK functions, water controls, notification tools, and updated example levels, alongside improvements to hosting, team setup, player management, lobby transitions, and Custom Experience presentation.

Audio, AI and Stability Improvements: Audio feedback has been improved across vehicles, weapons, voice-over, controllers, maps, and underwater gameplay, while AI navigation and behaviour, Campaign access, lighting, and visual-effect stability have also received further polish.

REDSEC and Ranked Battle Royale Updates: Rapid Royale arrives alongside a new Ranked Battle Royale season, while class equipment, Field Training, redeploy loadouts, armour plating, mission flow, loot presentation, Second Chance behaviour, and Ranked End of Round information have been updated.
CHANGELOG

Dev note: The team felt that anti-air cannons were not effective enough at punishing aggressive, mid-to-long-range fly-bys from aircraft. By increasing projectile velocity and reducing shell dispersion on Mobile AA, we aim to improve the consistency and effective range of ground-based anti-air, making it a more significant threat. Light attack aircraft, specifically the Scout Helicopter, are considered too effective vs infantry with their rockets. The changes in this update aim to curb this in the following ways:
Reducing Splash Damage: The 30% reduction in 70mm FFAR Light Rocket splash damage prevents one-hit kills on infantry at the most common engagement distances, requiring more precise aim from pilots.

Increasing Resupply Time: Lengthening the rocket pod resupply cooldown from 28 to 38 seconds forces pilots to be more selective with their attack runs, reducing their ability to perform "carpet-bombing" on ground targets.

We also wanted to improve counterplay, as low-altitude aircraft previously felt too safe from infantry threats. The initial goal is to make aircraft flying "below radar" more vulnerable to infantry lock-on missiles (MANPADS) to ensure that no altitude was completely safe and to reward infantry players for good positioning. However, in Battlefield Labs testing, it became clear that this change needed some more iterations before being ready for prime time. We'll keep you posted on these changes as we make progress.

Overall, we designed the balance updates in 2.1.1.0 to make anti-air systems more lethal and reliable, reduce the oppressive power of light aircraft against infantry, and ensure there are rewarding counter-tactics for both ground and air players.

Footstep Audio Improvements

Dev note: With 2.1.1.0, we're making several changes to the footstep audio, especially on enemies that are aimed at cases where enemies are less audible than expected through obstruction, especially in cases of tunnel intersections or corners. These changes bring up enemy footsteps in many situations, but we know that also includes some situations where that can add more confusion. The changes so far feel like a good step towards a better balance and compromise between the many edge cases and varying player expectations of how audible footsteps should be in our testing and reports. We continue to welcome your feedback, which will help to better balance and expand on the prioritization tech.
Enemy footstep audio now uses an improved priority system to better distinguish relevant nearby threats from less relevant enemies.
Footstep obstruction processing has been adjusted for more natural audio behaviour through the environment.
Footstep spatialisation and distance processing have been improved so footsteps sound more accurately positioned within the surrounding environment.
Friendly and enemy footsteps are now easier to distinguish from one another.
Reduced the effect of obstruction on footstep volume, making enemy footsteps easier to hear when partially obstructed.
Bots no longer drown inside vehicles while driving through shallow water.
Bots no longer enter vehicles while retreating from enemy-controlled objectives.
Bots now reload their gadgets more reliably.
Campaign can now be launched from the EA app while downloadable content is still downloading.

Dev note: A common point of player feedback over the past year of REDSEC has been that armor replating could at times feel a bit too slow or punishing. Considering this feedback as well as the introduction of the faster-paced Rapid Royale, we wanted to increase the speed at which players replate their armor across REDSEC, and subsequently scale back the effectiveness of the armor replating field training to keep things balanced appropriately.
Armor Plate application is now 20% faster by default in Battle Royale and Rapid Royale, with an additional 12% increase when using the Quick Plating Engineer Perk.
Battle Royale matchmaking now closes during the final 10 seconds of the pre-round lobby, preventing players from joining too late and missing the insertion window.
Battle Royale players at Field Training Level 1 or higher now redeploy with the EF88, PP-19, M121 A2, or Mini Scout, for Assault, Engineer, Support, and Recon respectively.
Players can now pick up the “Phantom Program Fragment” while carrying a vehicle keycard.
Players no longer become stuck when a teammate leaves the match while waiting for their Second Chance redeploy.
Class Training Paths and Gadgets have been rebalanced for Season 5.

Dev note: This was a calculated decision to focus on one strong, identifiable field training for each class, rather than split a class's effectiveness and identity among multiple paths. Parts of these training paths now live on in the existing paths below.
Hazmat Breacher and Drone Operator training paths have been removed from Assault and Recon, respectively
Existing Field Training Changes
Gadget 1: Assault Ladder
Gadget 2: High Explosive Grenade Launcher
Level 1: Reduced movement speed penalty when firing while moving.
Level 2: Passive health regeneration triggers 50% faster and provides a 50% improvement on healing. Revive sickness recovery time is reduced by 50%.
Level 3: High Explosive Launcher explosions generate 3 fused submunitions.
Level 4: Class gadget resupply rate increases by 10% with each improvement. Effect resets upon death.

Dev note: Assault class has been a popular pick for the latter half of REDSEC’s first year, primarily due to the amount of explosives it could output with its M320 HE gadget and the previous Level 2 training which increased grenade capacity. While this enabled generous destruction of cover and structures, it more often than not was primarily used to spam explosives directly at enemy players, resulting in a frustrating experience on the receiving end. These changes rein in the amount of explosives the class has access to at one time, and shift the focus of the class back onto gunfighting and breaching, with improved mobility and exceptional health regeneration ensuring Assault is the ultimate entry fragger.
Gadget 1: Repair Tool
Gadget 2: Aim-Guided Launcher
Level 1: Resistance to explosive damage is increased by 33%.
Level 2: Armor replating is 33% faster.
Level 3: Aim-Guided Launcher hits immobilized vehicles for 5s.
Level 4: Class gadget resupply rate increases by 10% with each improvement. Effect resets upon death.

Dev note: Engineer class was initially a popular class for REDSEC players, but this appeal quickly wore off as players discovered alternate ways of dealing with vehicles or felt underwhelmed by the class when there were no vehicular threats to tackle. The new Engineer training path shifts its emphasis towards making the class itself more tanky while still retaining effectiveness versus any vehicles that may appear. Faster armor replating and explosion resistance ensure survival in almost any situation, including those where getting up close with class-proficient SMGs is required to win that crucial 1v1 while defending your tank. The M136 AT will now also be aim-guided at round-start, assisting in the destruction of early-game threats like helicopters and ATPs to protect your squad, while the Repair Tool will continue to support friendly vehicles and open lootable safes.
Gadget 1: Supply Pouch
Gadget 2: Deployable Cover
Level 1: Improved weapon control when shooting from mounted positions.
Level 2: Drag downed soldiers 20% faster and revive them 2.5s quicker. Sprint 10% faster when under heavy fire.
Level 3: Reviving a teammate applies an armor plate to them. Placing Deployable Cover spawns a lootable armor plate.
Level 4: Class gadget resupply rate increases by 10% with each improvement. Effect resets upon death.

Dev note: Seeing the most change overall, feedback about the Supply Crate being too lethargic to use and the Smoke Launcher feeling outclassed by Smoke Grenades has been heard. Supply Pouches can now be used to heal and supply yourself or squadmates while on the run from the ring, or tossed mid-firefight as your squadmate holds out against advancing foes. The Deployable Cover can be used for impromptu protection for you and your squad while traversing between POIs or to fortify a destroyed building. The field training of Support reinforces the synergy of drag revives and the deployable cover, improving the prior's effectiveness and distributing armor plates with the latter. Between healing, reviving, ammunition, and armor, Support will be the true backbone of a squad.
Gadget 1: Motion Sensor
Gadget 2: Handheld Jammer
Level 1: Inflicting damage on enemies spots them, marking their position in-world and on the minimap.
Level 2: Downing an enemy spots others within a 25m radius for 5s.
Level 3: Handheld Jammer can disrupt Redeploy Points and Mobile Redeploys within its radius. Enemies who activated the redeploy device are revealed.
Level 4: Class gadget resupply rate increases by 10% with each improvement. Effect resets upon death.

Dev Note: The Recon class has consistently topped class pick rates throughout REDSEC’s lifespan thanks to its powerful intelligence gathering tools and training. The Recon Drone in particular became a borderline oppressive gadget that provided an unparalleled spotting ability at any range with near-zero risk, often ruining careful enemy rotations with a glance or feeling required to use before making a rotation yourself. For Season 5, the Recon class is now committed to localized intel gathering and intel sabotage in Battle Royale, trading the spotting abilities of the Drone for the disruptive capabilities of the Mobile Jammer, providing a direct counter to enemy Motion Sensors and redeploys. In combination with field training that gathers intel and denies enemy redeployments, the Recon will dominate the technology and information landscape of the Battlefield.

Dev note: As part of a general pass on the gunplay in REDSEC, it was important for us to ensure weapons are not overstepping their intended weapon archetypes. Particular weapons like the SG 553R, SCW-10, and KTS100 Mk8 have been at the forefront of highlighting this issue, and heavy-handed, targeted nerfs on these weapons (while potentially cathartic) would inevitably lead to similar weapons like the NVO-228E, KV9, and RPK-74M immediately filling their respective voids. Instead, these damage changes focus on ensuring weapons of a similar type are functioning as desired within their intended engagement ranges, but are less effective outside of those ranges. We will also have additional changes planned in future updates that will target other aspects of particular overperforming weapons.

Hello everyone,

Today we’re releasing our first major patch for Baldur’s Gate 3, addressing over 1000 bugs, balancing, flow issues and much, much more. Patch 1 is too big for our usual patch notes due to Steam’s character limit, so for the full notes head to this link:
Read the full Patch 1 patch notes (Note: Some of the entries might have spoilers!)

So what can you expect from this update? Well, we’ve eliminated issues like NPCs who sometimes spot you when they really shouldn’t be able to, floating items like mugs and newspapers that should abide the laws of gravity, and the conclusion to Shadowheart’s romance scene not triggering for some players, among others. With expansive systems come many unknowns, so our support team continues to work with you to relay any issues to us. Please don’t hesitate to reach out with further reports.
Patch 1 also tackles a few visual bugs, and sprinkles on more post-launch polish. We’re bringing back Short King Summer with better kissing contact for short races!

You won’t be waiting long for Patch 2, which is right around the corner. This update will feature significant performance improvements - but we’ll go into more detail about that closer to its release.
In the meantime, did you know that collectively you’ve played over 200,000,000 hours of Baldur's Gate 3 since launch? That’s over 22,000 years!
The most popular class choice is currently Paladin, followed by Sorcerer, while the award for least popular class goes to Cleric.

Human and Elf characters reign supreme in Faerûn, followed swiftly and unsurprisingly by Half-Elf. On the opposite end of the spectrum we find Dwarf, Gnome, Githyanki, and Halfling. We get it, they’re not exactly the most ethereal beauties of the Realms but they’d still form a rad metal band.
For now, as we focus on fixes, thank you for playing Baldur’s Gate 3 and continuing to share this adventure with us.

Fixed an issue where characters could get stuck in an infinite falling loop.
Fixed an issue with Marcus being resurrected by players hitting him with a dual-wield attack - the second hit will no longer revive him.
